dct_description_sm: As a piscivorous species, Yellow-billed Loons are top predators in lake ecosystems. They are harvested for human subsistence and are of concern because they may bioaccumulate contaminant loads (i.e. mercury, PCPs). In addition, they may be indicators of water quality and may provide insight into the movement of marine-derived nutrients and shifts in riparian or coastal communities.  Specific objectives include: 1) Determine triennial status and trends in density estimates of Yellow-billed Loons in selected sites of NW Alaskan Parks  during the breeding season (June); 2) Determine triennial trends in occupancy of Yellow-billed Loons in selected sites of NW Alaskan Parks during the breeding season (June); 3) Monitor the types and levels of common contaminants (mercury, PCPs) present in Yellow-billed Loons in selected sites of BELA and CAKR during the breeding season (June).
dct_title_s: Western Yellow-billed loons: National Park Service Alaska Region Inventory & Monitoring Program
